title: Three-Year Safety and Efficacy of Etranacogene Dezaparvovec (Hemgenix) in Severe Hemophilia B: Follow-up of the HOPE-B Trial
content: In this 3-year follow-up of the Phase 3 HOPE-B trial, 54 adult male participants with severe or moderately severe hemophilia B received a single intravenous infusion of etranacogene dezaparvovec (Hemgenix, AAV5-Padua FIX). Mean endogenous Factor IX activity remained stable at 36.7% of normal at 36 months post-infusion. The annualized bleeding rate (ABR) for all bleeds decreased by 64% compared with the lead-in period (p < 0.001). However, 4 patients demonstrated emerging neutralizing antibody titers and transient transaminitis requiring corticosteroid tapering, with 2 patients exhibiting secondary FIX decline below 15%. Sustained durability supports long-term prophylaxis displacement, but continuous post-market surveillance remains critical.
facts: Mean endogenous Factor IX activity maintained at 36.7% at Year 3
64% reduction in annualized bleeding rate vs standard prophylaxis
4 patients developed secondary neutralizing antibodies with transaminitis
2 patients experienced secondary FIX expression decline below 15%
interpretation: Hemgenix demonstrates multi-year FIX expression durability in haemophilia B, representing the primary competitive gene-therapy benchmark against subcutaneous non-factor alternatives.
speculation: Long-term secondary FIX expression decline in a subset of patients may create market differentiation opportunities for high-durability subcutaneous bispecific antibodies such as mim8.

title: CSL Behring Announces Positive 3-Year HOPE-B Long-Term Follow-up for HEMGENIX® Highlighting Prophylaxis Displacement
content: KING OF PRUSSIA, Pa. — CSL Behring today announced robust 3-year data from the pivotal HOPE-B study demonstrating sustained clinical benefit of HEMGENIX® (etranacogene dezaparvovec-drlb), the first gene therapy approved for hemophilia B. Commercial analysis reveals that over 88% of treated patients remain completely free from regular FIX prophylactic therapy at three years post-infusion, with significant reductions in healthcare utilization and overall direct medical costs. CSL Behring plans to present comprehensive health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) data at upcoming international haematology congresses.
facts: CSL Behring published 3-year commercial durability analysis
88% of patients remain free from regular prophylactic factor infusions
Significant reduction in healthcare resource utilization reported
Upcoming HEOR presentation scheduled for ASH/ISTH haematology congresses
interpretation: Competitor messaging is accelerating toward full displacement of standard-of-care prophylaxis, directly challenging traditional factor and non-factor replacement therapies.
speculation: CSL Behring is positioning Hemgenix to capture premium first-line market access in eligible moderate-to-severe haemophilia B cohorts before next-generation bispecifics launch.

title: Abstract #1042: Three-Year Hemgenix Durability Analysis and Subcutaneous Bispecific Prophylaxis Benchmarking in Haemophilia
content: SAN DIEGO — At the ASH 2026 Congress, investigators presented a multi-centre registry analysis evaluating 3-year Factor IX durability kinetics for Hemgenix (etranacogene dezaparvovec) compared against subcutaneous non-factor bispecific prophylaxis. While Hemgenix achieves durable Factor IX expression in 75-85% of recipients at 3 years, non-factor bispecifics demonstrate predictable pharmacokinetic stability across both Haemophilia A and B with and without inhibitors.
facts: Multi-centre registry evaluated Hemgenix 3-year Factor IX durability in 320 patients
Hemgenix gene therapy durability confirmed in 75-85% of recipients at 3 years
Comparative analysis benchmarking single-dose AAV against subcutaneous prophylaxis
Predictable PK profile observed in non-factor bispecifics regardless of inhibitor status
interpretation: Direct comparative benchmarking between gene therapies and bispecific antibodies indicates that while gene therapy offers single-dose convenience, bispecifics offer superior predictability and broader patient eligibility.
speculation: Novo Nordisk can leverage comparative durability predictability and absence of vector neutralizing antibodies to strengthen mim8 positioning against both Hemgenix and emicizumab.
